Computing Systems and Hardware: CPU
The processor that executes program instructions
RAM
Fast volatile memory holding data a program is actively using
Storage
Persistent memory such as an SSD that survives power loss
Operating system
Software managing hardware and running applications
Input device
Hardware sending data into a computer, such as a keyboard
Output device
Hardware presenting results, such as a monitor
Motherboard
The main board connecting a computer's components
GPU
A processor specialised for parallel work such as graphics or machine learning
Cache
Very fast memory holding recently used data close to the CPU
Moore's law
The observation that transistor density has roughly doubled every two years
Binary and Data Representation: Binary
The base-two number system computers use
Bit
A single binary digit, either 0 or 1
Byte
Eight bits, enough to store one character of text
Hexadecimal
Base sixteen, a compact way to write binary values
ASCII
An early standard mapping characters to numeric codes
Unicode
A standard encoding characters from every writing system
RGB color model
Representing colour as red, green, and blue intensity values
Pixel
The smallest addressable element of a digital image
Lossless compression
Reducing file size with no loss of information
Lossy compression
Reducing file size by discarding less noticeable data
Overflow
An error when a value exceeds the range its storage can hold
Algorithms and Pseudocode: A finite sequence of steps solving a problem
Plain-language description of an algorithm's logic
A diagram representing an algorithm's steps and decisions
Executing steps one after another in order
Choosing between paths based on a condition
Breaking a large problem into smaller manageable parts
Hiding unnecessary detail to focus on what matters
Spotting similarities that let one solution serve many cases
How well an algorithm uses time and memory
Checking each element in turn until the target is found
Repeatedly halving a sorted range to locate a value
Variables and Data Types: A named container holding a value that can change
A data type representing numbers with decimal points
A data type holding only true or false
Storing a value into a variable
A named value that must not change during execution
Changing a value from one data type to another
The region of a program where a variable is accessible
An agreed style for naming variables to keep code readable
Conditionals: Conditional statement
Code that runs only when a condition is true
If statement
The basic conditional executing a block when a test passes
Else clause
The block running when the condition is false
Else if
An additional condition checked when earlier ones fail
Comparison operator
A symbol comparing two values, such as greater than
Logical AND
An operator true only when both operands are true
Logical OR
An operator true when at least one operand is true
Logical NOT
An operator reversing a boolean value
Nested conditional
A conditional placed inside another conditional
Short-circuit evaluation
Skipping the second operand when the result is already decided
Boolean expression
An expression that evaluates to true or false
Loops: Loop
A structure repeating a block of code
For loop
A loop repeating a known number of times
While loop
A loop repeating as long as a condition stays true
Infinite loop
A loop whose condition never becomes false
Loop counter
A variable tracking how many iterations have run
Break statement
An instruction exiting a loop immediately
Continue statement
An instruction skipping to the next iteration
Nested loop
A loop placed inside another loop
Off-by-one error
A bug from looping one time too many or too few
Accumulator
A variable building up a running total across iterations
Iteration variable
The variable that changes each pass through a loop
Functions and Parameters: Function
A reusable named block of code performing a task
Parameter
A named input a function expects
Argument
The actual value passed to a function when calling it
Return value
The result a function sends back to its caller
Function call
The act of running a function by name
Local variable
A variable existing only inside the function that declares it
Global variable
A variable accessible throughout the program
Modularity
Organising a program into independent reusable pieces
Side effect
A change a function makes outside its own return value
Recursion
A function calling itself to solve a smaller version of a problem
Base case
The condition that stops a recursive function
Lists and Arrays: The position of an element, usually starting at zero
Numbering elements starting from zero rather than one
Adding an element to the end of a list
The number of elements it contains
Visiting each element of a collection in turn
An error from accessing a position that does not exist
A list of lists, useful for grids and tables
Extracting a portion of a list
Arranging elements into a defined order
Selecting only elements that meet a condition
Debugging and Testing: Bug
An error causing a program to behave incorrectly
Syntax error
A violation of the language's grammar, caught before running
Runtime error
An error occurring while the program executes
Logic error
Code that runs but produces the wrong result
Debugging
The process of finding and fixing errors
Test case
A specific input paired with its expected output
Edge case
An unusual input at the boundary of valid values
Print debugging
Inserting output statements to trace program state
Breakpoint
A marker pausing execution so state can be inspected
Rubber duck debugging
Explaining code aloud to expose faulty assumptions
Regression
A previously working feature broken by a new change
Introduction to Object-Oriented Programm: Object
A bundle of related data and the behaviour that acts on it
Class
A blueprint describing what objects of a type contain and do
Instance
A specific object created from a class
Attribute
A piece of data belonging to an object
Method
A function defined inside a class
Constructor
The special method that initialises a new object
Encapsulation
Bundling data with its methods and restricting outside access
Inheritance
A class acquiring the attributes and methods of a parent class
Polymorphism
Different classes responding to the same method call in their own way
Instantiation
The act of creating an object from a class
The Internet and Networks: The global network of interconnected computer networks
A numeric label identifying a device on a network
The system translating domain names into IP addresses
A small unit of data transmitted across a network
An agreed set of rules governing data exchange
The protocol used to request and deliver web pages
The maximum data a connection can carry per second
The delay before data begins transferring
A computer providing data or services to other machines
A computer requesting data or services from a server
A device directing packets between networks
Cybersecurity and Digital Citizenship: Encryption
Encoding data so only authorised parties can read it
Public key encryption
A scheme using a shared public key and a private key
Phishing
Deceptive messages tricking people into revealing credentials
Malware
Software written to damage or gain unauthorised access
Firewall
A barrier filtering network traffic by defined rules
Two-factor authentication
Requiring a second proof of identity beyond a password
Strong password
A long, unique password that is hard to guess or crack
Digital footprint
The trail of data a person leaves online
Data privacy
Control over how personal information is collected and used
Intellectual property
Legal rights over original creative and technical work
Creative Commons
Licences letting creators grant specific reuse permissions
Algorithmic bias
Systematic unfairness produced by a system's data or design
